evals.name: name-the-effect
evals.prompt: What's the word for when a menu opens and kind of grows out of the button you clicked, instead of just appearing in the middle of itself?
evals.expected_output: The skill reads for the sensation and answers with the term first: an origin-aware animation, with the transform origin set at the trigger. It gives a one-line definition and names a close alternate (scale in) with the line between them.
expectations: The answer leads with the term origin-aware animation, or names the transform origin set at the trigger
The answer gives a one-line definition of the term
The answer names at least one close alternate term and says how it differs
The answer writes no animation code
evals.source: reference/motion.md movement-and-transforms (Origin-aware animation, Transform origin), written for this suite

evals.name: kerning-not-tracking
evals.prompt: In our logo the A and the V look too far apart, but every other letter is spaced fine. What is it called when you adjust just the space between those two letters?
evals.expected_output: The skill answers kerning: the space between one specific pair of letters. It tells it apart from tracking (letter spacing applied evenly across a run of text), and does not coin a term.
expectations: The answer names kerning as the term
The answer says kerning adjusts the space between a specific pair of letters
The answer names tracking or letter spacing as the near-synonym and says it applies evenly across a whole run of text
The answer does not invent a new term
evals.source: the skill's reverse lookup and near-synonym rule; kerning versus tracking is the standard typographic distinction, written for this suite

evals.name: clip-versus-mask
evals.prompt: For a before and after image reveal, should I be asking for a clip or a mask? I think they're the same thing.
evals.expected_output: The skill separates the two terms on the axis that differs: a clip cuts the element to a shape with a hard edge, a mask hides or reveals parts with a shape or gradient and can have soft edges. It names the before and after slider as the term for the draggable divider.
expectations: The answer says clip and mask are not the same
The answer says a clip has a hard edge and a mask can have soft or gradient edges
The answer names the before and after slider, or says either can drive a before and after reveal
evals.source: reference/motion.md polish (Clip, Mask, Before / after slider), written for this suite

evals.name: no-term-fits-asks-for-image
evals.prompt: You know that thing some apps do where the whole screen sort of breathes and the colors drift when it's idle? I don't know how else to describe it. What's it called?
evals.expected_output: The skill names the closest terms it holds (an idle animation, an ambient float or pulse) and labels them an approximation, does not coin a new term, and asks for a reference image, a recording or a link to an example to pin it down.
expectations: The answer names a close existing term such as idle animation, ambient motion, float or pulse
The answer says the term is an approximation or the closest match
The answer asks for a reference image, a screen recording or a link to an example
The answer does not present a coined term as an established name
evals.why_hard: A vague description pulls the model toward a confident invented label; the case needs the closest real term marked as approximate and a request for a reference
evals.source: the skill's no-term-fits rule and reference/motion.md looping-and-ambient, written for this suite
